zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical cross-check: supplied NINJAL Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida (CC BY 4.0). The scan, not the lexical index, determines the transcription. Source: https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; license: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

lines.note: Completes Tçu-cayeuo ſuru from f481: placing props against a wall. This is running text, not a second copy of the preceding page's catchword; pare- continues parede below.

runs.text: de, ou outra couſa que eſtà pera cair. No Xi-

lines.note: Completes parede and includes anything about to fall. No is wholly italic, correcting the provisional font split; Xi- begins the regional name Ximo, not an independent example word.

Completes Ximo and gives the regional alternative expression for placing a support. The final cǒ has a clear caron rather than the OCR's tilde; the locally italic treatment is retained for human typeface review.
This verb sense concerns something being obstructed or unable to proceed. The Portuguese explanatory i introduces a fuller definition, beginning with the negative Não.

runs.text: poder ir por diante, como a porta que não ſe po-

lines.note: The obstruction prevents forward movement, like a door that cannot close. The printed po- continues pode on the next physical row.

runs.text: de fechar, hum pao comprido que não pode en-

lines.note: Completes the door example and introduces a long piece of wood that cannot enter. En- begins entrar below; the historical pao is not given an unprinted nasal mark.

runs.text: trar todo nalgum lugar, por embaçar diante,

lines.note: The timber cannot enter fully because it meets an obstruction ahead. The source's embaçar has a cedilla, and the clause continues into the following examples.
Shoku ga tsukayuru applies the obstruction sense to food, explained as already being full. The visible gap in Eſtar ja is restored; far- continues farto below.

runs.text: to de maneira que não pode o estamago leuar

lines.note: Completes farto: the stomach cannot take any more. The printed historical estamago is retained rather than modernized to estomago, and the provisional st classification is not globally changed.
Completes the food example, then gives ki or mune ga tsukayuru, a feeling of constriction in the chest. The alternative marker l is not Japanese; Eſ- begins Eſtar below.
The heart or chest feels oppressed and constricted. This completes the preceding example, retaining the printed nasal vowel and cedilla in coração.
Tsuchi denotes earth or clay. The brief gloss is wholly Portuguese italic, distinct from the homonymous hammer entry that follows.

runs.text: Maço, ou maçete de pao, ou martello

lines.note: This tsuchi is a wooden mallet or an iron hammer. Both cedillas in Maço and maçete are visible; martello retains its printed doubled l.
Completes the iron-hammer definition, then gives sayezuchi as a pounding tool. The Portuguese begins a rice-pounding use, continued below.
Completes the rice-pestle description and adds a carpenter's mallet. Carpinteiro is printed in full here rather than with the abbreviation found on f480.
Tsuchikure is a clod of earth. Torrão is treated as the complete italic Portuguese noun, correcting the provisional isolated roman T while preserving the printed nasal vowel.
Tsuchikurebato is glossed as a turtledove. The unusually formed compound is retained as printed rather than replaced by a modern bird name.
Tsuchidan and dodan denote an earthen step or raised platform. The alternative marker l and the historical spelling Degrao remain unchanged.

runs.text: ou lugar mais aleuãtado pera por algũa couſa.

lines.note: The platform is a raised place on which to put something. Aleuãtado corrects OCR alcuãtado, retaining the nasal abbreviation and the historical pera.
Tsuchido first denotes a door coated or blocked with clay. The paragraph sign introduces another sense, continued below.

runs.text: Porta, ou portal do pateo, ou Niua.

lines.note: The additional sense is a courtyard or garden gate. Niua is a Japanese term embedded in Portuguese and is retained in its locally italic form for whole-word font review.
Tsuchina is described as an herb resembling wild lettuces. The damaged but surviving top and stem of T restore the omitted initial; alfaçes retains its visible cedilla.
Completes alfaçes ſiluestres, wild lettuces. The short continuation remains separate, with the provisional st rendering preserved rather than globally normalized.
Tsuchinabe is an earthenware cooking pot. The complete entry is confined to this row and is distinct from the herb description above.
Tsuchinoe and tsuchinoto are names used in the calendar's year cycle. The final an continues Annos below without a supplied terminal hyphen.

runs.text: nos conforme ao calendario de Iapão.

lines.note: Completes annos and identifies the Japanese calendar. Iapão is the Portuguese country name, not a Japanese word requiring typeface-term marking.

Tsukōmatsuri is explained by tsukaye tatematsuru, respectfully serving. The caron and the separate full stop after ru are retained; the explanatory i has a visible comma rather than the provisional period.

runs.text: Seruir honrando a peßoa aquem ſe ſerue.

lines.note: The service honours the person being served. The source's close aquem and peßoa form are retained; the final upright S is the written-register label, not part of the italic definition.
Tsukubai describes squatting humbly. The principal forms show carons, and humil- begins the adverb completed below.
Completes humildemente, the humble manner of squatting. The short row remains an independent physical continuation.

runs.text: Hũa laya de armas de hastea com-

lines.note: Tsukubō is described as a kind of long-shafted weapon. Hũa and laya have a visible word boundary, correcting their provisional fusion; com- begins comprida below.

runs.text: prida com o cabo atraueſado, & forrado com

lines.note: Completes the long shaft and describes its transverse, covered end. The source's single long s in atraueſado is preserved, and the covering is specified on the next row.

runs.text: muitas pontas de que vſão quando prendem al-

lines.note: The historical description mentions many points and use in apprehending someone. Al- begins alguem below; the row remains part of the tsukubō definition.
Completes alguem and gives the purpose as subduing the person. The printed ſujugar is retained without adding the b of a modern spelling.
Tsukubushi and tsububushi are alternative forms for the kneecap. The second form recalls the f480 entry; the scan, not that parallel, determines the present letters.
Tsukumo is labelled poetic and described as a sea herb. The initial T corrects OCR r; the historical botanical description is retained without imposing a modern species identification.
Tsukumogami is given a poetic gloss of ninety-nine years. The explicit number and Annos are preserved rather than replacing the source's definition with another modern sense of the word.
Tsukune means forming rounded balls by hand. Pilouros is the source's Portuguese noun, with its material examples continued on the next row.

runs.text: mãos como de neue, de barro, ou maßa.

lines.note: Snow, clay and dough illustrate the hand-formed balls. The occurrence-specific mãos, historical neue and the ß-shaped type in maßa are retained.
Tsukunoi means making satisfaction or restitution. Both abbreviated principal forms have circumflexes, unlike the carons in earlier entries; the Portuguese st rendering is retained as aligned.

runs.text: ¶ Item, per met. Concertar o beneplacito dal

lines.note: The figurative sense concerns restoring another person's goodwill or satisfaction. The word dalguem is divided after dal without a secure printed hyphen.

runs.text: guem, ou dar ſatisfação à peßoa agrauada.

lines.note: Completes dalguem and specifies giving satisfaction to the aggrieved person. The scan supports continuous ſatisfação, correcting the OCR's internal space; à and peßoa are retained.
The noun tsukunoi is payment or satisfaction. Its Portuguese ſatisfação is one word; Toga- begins the example about making amends for wrongdoing.
Completes toga no tsukunoi wo suru, making amends for faults or sins. The first u in tçucunoiuo corrects OCR n, and the Portuguese Satisfazer is visibly continuous.

Completes the translation as satisfaction for sins. The abraded word is read peccados, not OCR paeados; the two-c spelling is supported by surviving types and a clearer repetition in the next column, but the damaged middle remains a nonblocking caveat.
Tsukuri is making or doing. The principal parts and the abbreviated Cõmummente are preserved; the author begins a qualification about the kinds of things made.

runs.text: de couſas que ſe fazem com as mãos. ¶

lines.note: The verb is commonly used of things made by hand. Vô- begins the woman-and-eyebrows example continued at the top of the next column; its locally weak accent is retained provisionally rather than regularized from the expected Japanese word.
Completes the woman-and-eyebrows example begun with Vô- in the preceding column. The Portuguese describes adorning herself by arranging the eyebrows; mo- begins molher below.
Completes the eyebrow translation, with as ſobrancelhas correcting the OCR's merged aeſobrancelhas. Iyeuo then introduces making or building a house.
Iye wo tsukuru means building a house. The faint initial E in Edificar corrects OCR F; ta wo tçu- begins the example of cultivating fields.

Completes ta wo tsukuru, cultivating the paddy fields. Cultiuar corrects Caltiuar. Deustẽ- begins the next upright Japanese sentence about God and heaven and earth; its close printed spacing is retained.
Completes tenchi wo naki tokoro yori tsukuri tamō, the creation of heaven and earth from nothing. The caron in tamǒ is visible; De- begins the Portuguese translation, not another Japanese fragment.

runs.text: os criou o ceo, & terra de nada. ¶

lines.note: Completes Deos and translates creation from nothing. Toqi- starts the next example concerning a war cry; ceo remains the printed historical spelling.
Toki wo or toki no koe wo tsukuru means raising a war cry. The alternative marker l is editorial, and gri- starts grita below.

runs.text: ta como quem dà Santiago na guerra. ¶

lines.note: The gloss compares the shouting to giving the Santiago battle cry. The scan reads quem and Santiago, correcting quemr and Sanitiago; Tçu- begins the next example.
Completes tsumi wo tsukuru, committing sins. The clearer peccados supplies a comparison for the damaged occurrence in c1-l045; Xi- begins shi, the verse example below.
Shi wo tsukuru is composing Chinese-style verse in this gloss. The abbreviation hũs and the close daChina spacing are retained rather than normalized.
Michi wo tsukuru illustrates making roads or paths. The complete upright example and its italic translation occupy this physical row.
Kotoba wo tsukuru is composing or inventing words. The abbreviated inuẽ continues into tar below; the small terminal mark is retained as the aligned period rather than replaced by an inferred hyphen.

runs.text: tar palauras. ¶ Item, Fingir, ou contra-

lines.note: Completes inventing words, then introduces the sense of feigning or counterfeiting. The printed contra- continues contrafazer on the next row.

runs.text: fazer algũa couſa. Mas commũmente ſe vſa

lines.note: Completes contrafazer and begins a usage qualification. Both algũa and commũmente retain their occurrence-specific nasal marks.

runs.text: neste ſentido compoſto como ſe verà a baixo.

lines.note: The author says this sense is generally used in compounds, illustrated below. The grave in verà and the separate a baixo are preserved; the st class in neste is not globally regularized.

Tsukuriage means raising something by building it. The worn a between i and g is recovered in Tçucuriague rather than omitted as in OCR Tçucurigue; it remains a nonblocking caveat, with the following riaguete providing a clearer comparison.
Completes raising by construction and introduces a building with two or three storeys. Nicai and ſangaiuo remain upright; the example verb is divided at tçucu-.

Completes tsukuriagete. The translation describes raising upper floors, with the tilde in Aleuantãdo, abbreviated hũ and close dousſobrados retained. The nasally abbreviated participle is not given a stress accent.

Tsukuriawase means acting or making something in concert. The worn a in the headword is recovered from residual strokes and the repeated examples. The tall ſ in the aligned principal form ſuru is retained, matching historical awasuru; Vt is italic.

Completes toki wo tsukuriawasuru: the opposing sides raise their cries together. The weak u after curia is retained as u rather than OCR r, consistent with the surviving stroke and the repeated compound.
Specifies the enemies on one side and the other. The next example begins tsukuriawa-, continued below; the Portuguese hũa retains its nasal abbreviation.

runs.text: Ir de companhia com algũa cou

lines.note: Completes tsukuriawasete mairu, going together by arrangement. Companhia and com remain separate printed words; the unhyphenated division cou/ſa is retained rather than supplied with an inferred hyphen.

runs.text: ſa com poſta, ou tramada pera enganar a alguẽ,

lines.note: Completes couſa and describes a contrived arrangement to deceive someone. The aligned internal spacing com poſta is retained, and the final alguẽ remains abbreviated.
Adds that the concerted arrangement may serve another purpose. This brief italic row finishes the example before the next flush-left headword.
Tsukurikake is beginning to make something or leaving its construction unfinished. The printed principal parts are retained; the second alternative continues below.
Completes making without finishing, then gives a war-cry example. The source separates tçucuri from ca-, and Vt belongs to the italic apparatus.

runs.text: Começar a dar grita de hũa parte dos

lines.note: Completes tsukuri kakuru, starting the shout on one side of the opposing forces. The initial quru remains on this physical row, and hũa retains its tilde.

runs.text: inimigos. ¶ Item, Fabricar junto de outra

lines.note: Finishes the war-cry example and adds construction beside another building. The paragraph sign separates these senses without introducing a new headword.

runs.text: caſa, ou obra, demaneira que fique como hũa ſô.

lines.note: The new building joins another so that they form a single whole. Demaneira remains close-set; hũa and ſô are separate. The final accented vowel is italic with its word, correcting the provisional isolated roman ô without modernizing its mark.

runs.text: ¶ Itẽ, Fabricar demaneira que fique a obra, ou

lines.note: Another construction sense describes a structure spanning different levels. Itẽ remains abbreviated; the printed a obra spacing is retained.

runs.text: edificio parte embaixo, & parte ſobre algũa

lines.note: The building is partly below and partly on raised ground. The source's embaixo, the long s in ſobre and the abbreviation algũa are retained.

runs.text: terra aleuantada, ou ſobre o mar, &c.

lines.note: Completes the raised-ground description and adds a structure over the sea. Ou and ſobre remain separate words, and the entry ends before the next headword.
Tsukurikatame means making something firm or strong. The visibly printed de before dura below is anomalous Portuguese but is retained, not silently deleted to improve the sentence.

Continues the hardening or strengthening sense, followed by an additional finishing sense. Dura is genuine body text after the preceding printed de; the anomaly is not repaired by changing the line division.
Completes the additional sense of finishing a work or building. The abbreviation algũa and the historical edificio remain unchanged.
Tsukurikome concerns inserting or setting something with skill. The definition begins here and is illustrated by setting a precious stone below.

runs.text: algũa couſa dentro noutra como quem encastoa

lines.note: The object is set inside another, like someone setting a gem. The final a in encastoa is visible: this is a complete present-tense verb, not the provisional divided encasto-; no physical row is missing here.
The gem-setting comparison ends, then the quotation starts sono uchi ni, within it. The printed ſu- begins sugureta on the following row.

Completes sugureta and describes fine pearls or jewels of excellent colour and quality set inside. Enlargement supports the aligned xinano despite the worn arch of its first n; meixuuo has no supplied extra i after x, and the terminal division is retained.

Ta completes the quoted verb; Mon. is the upright citation label. The Portuguese begins setting excellent jewels inside. The label is marked for typeface review, while the aligned st rendering in Encastoarão remains unchanged.
Completes excellentes and the quotation's translation about various precious stones. The historical precioſas and the physical division remain unchanged.
Tsukurigane is false or artificially compounded metal. The headword's damaged n is retained from the aligned reading; arti- begins the adverb continued below.
Completes artificioſamente and gives false silver as an example. The surviving wording supports the metal imitation sense rather than a new entry.
Tsukurigao is an assumed or counterfeit facial expression. Fingido corrects OCR fngido; the provisional st rendering in Rosto is retained under the deferred ligature review.
Tsukuridashi means making anew or bringing something into being. The printed ſu and aita principal parts are retained, with the first gloss continued below.

runs.text: inuentar algũa couſa de mãos. ¶ Item, Fin

lines.note: Completes inventing something by hand, then introduces feigning or fabrication. Fin continues as gir on the next row; no secure terminal hyphen is visible, so none is supplied from the word's continuation.

runs.text: gir de ſi, ou de nouo algũa couſa. Vt,

lines.note: Completes Fingir and describes inventing something oneself or anew. Vt is wholly italic, while Tçu is wholly upright, correcting the provisional partial italic T. The lower curidaite is separate catchword furniture and continues the example's historical -aite form.

The native crop reads curidaite, not curidaſu or OCR curidaica. Together with Tçu above, it gives the historical -aite form of tçucuridaxi, consistent with the printed past form aita. This is a catchword, not a second body continuation.
